title: Four-scene solar data explainer driven by a CSV
prompt:
Produce a 24-second animated data explainer for the Meridia Energy Agency about rooftop solar. The data is in solar.csv (columns year, province, capacity_mw, share_pct: installed rooftop capacity in megawatts and the share of homes with rooftop solar, in percent) for the eight provinces of Meridia from 2015 to 2024. Every number on screen must come from the CSV.

Format: 1280x720, 30 fps, exactly 24 s (720 frames). Four scenes of 6 s each. The scene boundaries are at 6, 12 and 18 s, and each boundary is a 0.5 s transition centred on it (5.75 to 6.25 s, 11.75 to 12.25 s, 17.75 to 18.25 s):
- at 6 s a cross-dissolve;
- at 12 s a push: scene 2 slides out to the left while scene 3 slides in from the right, ease-in-out;
- at 18 s an iris: scene 4 is revealed inside a circle that grows from the centre of the frame until it covers everything.

Scene 1, 'Capacity is soaring': a line chart of national capacity (the sum over the provinces) per year, with a y axis from 0 to 3,000 MW (gridlines every 500) and a year axis. The line draws itself at a constant pace from 0.5 s to 5.0 s, reaching year Y at t = 0.5 + 0.5 × (Y − 2015) s. Each year gets a dot when the line reaches it, and a label at the tip shows the value of the latest year reached, formatted like 1,234 MW. When the line reaches the first year whose total is at least double the 2015 total, a callout 'Doubled by YYYY' (with that year) attaches to that point and stays.

Scene 2, 'The provincial race': a horizontal bar chart race of capacity_mw for all eight provinces, sorted descending, each province in its own fixed color, with name and value labels. It shows 2015 until 6.5 s, then advances one year every 0.5 s (year Y exactly at t = 6.5 + 0.5 × (Y − 2015) s, so 2024 at 11.0 s), with values interpolating and bars gliding to their new rank. A large year counter shows the integer year.

Scene 3, 'Homes going solar': a tile map with one rounded square per province, arranged like a map on a 4-column grid: row 1 Highmark (column 2) and Farrow Hills (column 3); row 2 Galen Plains, Aldena, Corvel and Dunmore (columns 1 to 4); row 3 Brisa Coast (column 2) and Estrel Valley (column 3). Each tile is filled by its share_pct bin: under 10 #FEF3C7, 10 to under 20 #FDE68A, 20 to under 30 #FBBF24, 30 to under 40 #F59E0B, 40 and over #B45309, and is labelled with the province name and its share (like 12.5%). Show 2015 until 13.0 s, cross-fade the colors to 2020 over 13.0 to 14.0 s, hold, cross-fade to 2024 over 15.0 to 16.0 s and hold to the end of the scene. A year label reads 2015, 2020 or 2024 (switching at the midpoint of each fade), and a legend lists the five bins.

Scene 4, 'Ten years in four numbers': four KPI cards that enter one by one at 18.5, 18.9, 19.3 and 19.7 s (rising and fading in over 0.4 s), each number counting up from 0 over 1.0 s with an ease-out: total capacity in 2024 (MW); growth since 2015 (percent, whole number, like +57%); fastest-growing province (the largest ratio of 2024 to 2015 capacity, shown as its name and the ratio with one decimal, like ×1.8); and the number of provinces where at least 30% of homes had solar in 2024 (as N of 8).

Across all scenes the frame keeps the same chrome, which does not take part in the transitions: a scene indicator at the top right with four dots (the current scene's dot highlighted) and the source line 'Source: Meridia Energy Agency (sample data)' at the bottom left. Give each scene its title, use Inter, and keep a consistent editorial style (dark or light).

rubric.criterion: Scene 1 values: a frame at about 5.5 s shows the national line with ten points from 2015 to 2024 that match the CSV totals (spot-check at least three against the y axis or labels: 855 MW in 2015, 1,845 MW in 2020, 2,772 MW in 2024), and the tip label reads 2,772 MW.

The line draws on the stated schedule: a frame at about 2.6 s shows the line through 2019 (tip label 1,643 MW) but not yet reaching 2020, and the callout 'Doubled by 2020' is attached to the 2020 point from about 3.0 s on (absent at 2.6 s; any other year is wrong).

Scene 2 final state (frame at about 11.5 s, year 2024): all eight bars in this order with these values: Brisa Coast 650, Aldena 505, Galen Plains 412, Corvel 385, Dunmore 270, Estrel Valley 225, Highmark 180, Farrow Hills 145.

Rank swaps happen at the right years, with the year counter agreeing: at about 7.5 s (2017) Corvel is still above Brisa Coast and Estrel Valley above Galen Plains; at about 8.0 s (2018) Brisa Coast is above Corvel and Galen Plains above Estrel Valley; at about 9.0 s (2020) Aldena still leads; at about 9.5 s (2021) Brisa Coast has taken first place.

Scene 3 tile colors follow the bins: at about 17.0 s (2024) Brisa Coast is #B45309; Corvel and Galen Plains #F59E0B; Aldena, Dunmore and Highmark #FBBF24; Estrel Valley and Farrow Hills #FDE68A. At about 14.5 s (2020) Brisa Coast is #FBBF24, Farrow Hills and Highmark #FEF3C7 and the other five #FDE68A. Tiles show name and share (e.g. Corvel 30.2% in 2024).

The tile map uses the specified arrangement (Highmark and Farrow Hills on top; Galen Plains, Aldena, Corvel, Dunmore in the middle row; Brisa Coast and Estrel Valley at the bottom) with a five-bin legend; colors cross-fade (a frame at about 13.5 s shows in-between colors) and the year label reads 2015 at 12.8 s, 2020 at 14.5 s and 2024 at 17.0 s.

Scene 4 KPI values are exactly (frame at about 23 s): 2,772 MW total capacity; +224% growth; fastest-growing Highmark ×6.0 (not Brisa Coast, the largest absolute gain); 3 of 8 provinces at 30% or more.

KPI cards enter one at a time: a frame at about 19.0 s shows the first card with its number still counting and at most two cards present (the third and fourth absent); all four numbers are final by about 20.8 s.

The three transitions have the right kind and timing: the frame at 6.0 s blends scenes 1 and 2 (cross-dissolve); the frame at 12.0 s shows scenes 2 and 3 side by side mid-push; the frame at 18.0 s shows scene 4 inside a circle over scene 3; frames at about 5.6, 6.4, 11.6, 12.4, 17.6 and 18.4 s each show a single scene.

Persistent chrome: the scene indicator highlights dot 1 at 3 s, dot 2 at 9 s, dot 3 at 15 s and dot 4 at 21 s, and it and the source line 'Source: Meridia Energy Agency (sample data)' stay fixed in place (not dissolved, pushed or masked) during the transitions.
Every sampled frame is readable: axis, value and tile labels do not collide, race bars never overlap at rest, KPI numbers fit their cards, and nothing is clipped at the frame edges.

Consistent editorial design across the four scenes: one type family with a clear title/label hierarchy, fixed province colors in the race, the specified amber scale in the tile map, and eased motion without jumps or flicker.

title: Karaoke lyric video synced to a word-timing file
prompt:
Make a karaoke-style lyric video for the song described in lyrics.json: it gives the title, the artist and six lines, each a list of words with start and end times in seconds. The highlighting must follow those times exactly, the way a karaoke player would.

Format: 1280x720, 30 fps, exactly 20 s (600 frames), no audio needed.

Title card, 0 to 2 s: the song title large with the artist below it. It fades out from 1.6 to 2.0 s while the lyric area fades in.

Lyric area: the current line is centred horizontally at y = 330 in a 64 px bold face; the next line is centred below it at y = 430, in 40 px at about 45% opacity. Line 1 is current from 1.6 s. A line stays current until its last word ends; at that moment the next line takes over with a 0.3 s animation: the finished line slides up and fades out, the next line moves up into the current slot while growing to 64 px and full opacity, and the line after it fades in as the new next line. The last line has no next line.

Word states on the current line:
- not yet sung: light grey #CBD5E1;
- being sung (from its start to its end time): a karaoke wipe, the word fills with yellow #FACC15 from left to right in proportion to the elapsed fraction of its duration (at the midpoint of a word exactly its left half is yellow);
- sung: solid yellow.

Instrumental break: when the gap between the last word of one line and the first word of the next is longer than 2.0 s, show three lead-in dots above the waiting line during the last 1.5 s before its first word; one dot goes out every 0.5 s, the last one exactly when the first word starts.

HUD: a 6 px progress bar along the bottom edge, filled in proportion to t / 20; above its right end the elapsed time as m:ss.t truncated to tenths (for example 0:07.4); at the top right 'Line N of 6' for the current line.

Ending: after the last word keep the finished line on screen, then fade the whole lyric area out from 19.5 to 20.0 s.

Style: a deep night background (for example a vertical gradient from #1E1B4B to #0F172A) with a few softly glowing lantern circles drifting slowly upward behind the text; Inter throughout; the lyrics must stay the most readable thing on screen.

rubric.criterion: At 3.30 s line 1 is current: 'Light' and 'a' are solid yellow, 'lantern' is partly filled from the left (between about 45% and 65% of its width yellow), 'on the water' is grey, and line 2 'send it drifting past the pier' is shown dimmed and smaller below.

At 6.00 s line 2 is current with 'send' and 'it' yellow, 'drifting' mostly filled (more than about 70% but not all) and 'past the pier' grey; at 15.50 s line 5 is current with 'when the tide' yellow, 'turns' filled about halfway (35% to 65%) and 'in the morning' grey.

At 8.30 s line 3 'every ember is a letter' is current with 'every' yellow and 'ember' a bit over half filled; at 18.90 s line 6 'follow every light back home' is current with 'follow every light back' yellow, 'home' about two-thirds filled, and no next line below it.
Words are never highlighted early: at 2.30 s no word of line 1 has any yellow, and at 12.05 s only the first word 'saying' of line 4 has started filling while the rest of line 4 is grey.

Line changes follow the rule: at 4.60 s line 1 is still current (its last word 'water' partly filled); a frame at about 4.80 s shows the takeover in progress (line 1 moving up and fading, line 2 moving up and growing); by 5.00 s line 2 is current and line 1 is gone.

Lead-in dots before line 4: at 10.20 s line 4 'saying I am always here' is current, all grey, with no dots; three dots at 10.75 s, two at 11.25 s, one at 11.75 s, and none at 12.10 s. No lead-in dots appear before any other line.

HUD is correct: the timecode reads 0:07.4 at about 7.45 s and 0:13.1 at about 13.15 s (±0.1 s); the counter reads 'Line 4 of 6' at 10.2 s and 'Line 6 of 6' at 18.9 s; the progress bar is about 37% full at 7.45 s and nearly full at the end.
The title card at about 1.0 s shows 'Lanterns on the Water' large with 'Marlow & the Low Tide' below it; by 2.2 s it is gone and line 1 (all grey) and line 2 (dimmed) are showing.
Ending: at 19.40 s line 6 is entirely yellow; the last frame (about 19.97 s) shows the lyric area faded out or nearly so.

Layout follows the brief: the current line is centred around y = 330 and the next line around y = 430 in smaller, dimmer type; the longest line 'when the tide turns in the morning' fits inside the frame with at least 64 px side margins; the HUD never overlaps the lyrics.

Polished look: a night gradient with softly glowing lanterns drifting behind the text without hurting legibility, a clean karaoke wipe edge with no flicker between consecutive frames, and consistent Inter typography.

title: Time-lapse world clocks across midnight
prompt:
Create an 18-second time-lapse of three world clocks for the opening titles of 'Night Shift', a documentary about people who work while others sleep.

Format: 1280x720, 30 fps, exactly 18 s (540 frames).

Simulated time: at t = 0 it is 20:00 on Friday 13 March 2026 in London, and simulated time runs at 20 minutes per video second, so London shows 20:00 + 20 × t minutes and reaches 02:00 on Saturday at the very end. The other clocks derive from London: New York is London minus 4 hours and Tokyo is London plus 9 hours (use these fixed offsets; no daylight-saving logic).

Three clocks side by side, left to right: New York, London, Tokyo. Each clock has:
- the city name above it with a small offset tag (UTC−4, UTC+0, UTC+9);
- an analog face with 12 hour ticks and hour and minute hands that move continuously: the minute hand sweeps a full turn every 3 s and the hour hand creeps accordingly, never jumping from hour to hour; no second hand;
- a digital 24-hour readout HH:MM below the face showing the local time truncated to the minute, drawn with fixed-width digit cells so the readout never jitters sideways;
- the local weekday and date below that, formatted like Fri 13 Mar.

Day and night: a face is light (#F8FAFC with dark hands and ticks) while its local time is from 06:00 up to but not including 18:00, and dark (#1E293B with light hands and ticks) otherwise. It switches exactly at those instants, and shows a small sun icon when light and a crescent moon when dark.

At the top: the title 'Night Shift' and the subtitle 'Three cities, six hours · 1 second = 20 minutes'. At the bottom: a horizontal timeline labelled 'London time' with seven evenly spaced ticks labelled 20:00, 21:00, 22:00, 23:00, 00:00, 01:00 and 02:00, and a playhead that moves along it at constant speed, on 20:00 at the start and on 02:00 at the end. A thin vertical marker above the 00:00 tick is labelled 'Midnight in London'.

Style: calm, cinematic and legible: a deep blue-black background (#0B1020 to #111827), Inter, generous spacing, faces about 240 px across. Only the clocks and the playhead move.

rubric.criterion: Digital readouts are correct: at 4.5 s New York 17:30, London 21:30, Tokyo 06:30; at 7.25 s New York 18:25, London 22:25, Tokyo 07:25 (±1 minute).
Analog hands agree with the time at 4.5 s: all three minute hands point straight down (half past), and the hour hands sit halfway between 5 and 6 (New York), 9 and 10 (London) and 6 and 7 (Tokyo).

Day/night switching is exact: Tokyo's face is dark at 2.9 s and light at 3.1 s; New York's face is light at 5.9 s and dark at 6.1 s; London's face is dark throughout (check 1, 9 and 17 s); each face shows a sun when light and a crescent moon when dark.

The date changes at midnight: at 11.9 s London reads 23:58 (±1 minute) with Fri 13 Mar and at 12.1 s it reads 00:02 (±1 minute) with Sat 14 Mar; New York shows Fri 13 Mar and Tokyo Sat 14 Mar for the whole video.
The final frame (about 17.97 s) reads New York 21:59, London 01:59, Tokyo 10:59 (±1 minute), and the playhead is on (within a few pixels of) the 02:00 tick.

Hands move continuously: between consecutive frames the minute hands advance about 4° and the hour hands a fraction of a degree; comparing 8.0 and 8.5 s, the hour hands moved about 5° and never jump by a whole hour step.

The timeline has seven evenly spaced ticks labelled 20:00 to 02:00 with the 'London time' label; the playhead moves at constant speed (over the 23:00 tick at 9.0 s and over 00:00 at 12.0 s), and the 'Midnight in London' marker sits on the 00:00 tick.
Text is exact: title 'Night Shift', subtitle 'Three cities, six hours · 1 second = 20 minutes', and city names New York, London, Tokyo in that order with tags UTC−4, UTC+0 and UTC+9.

The three clocks are equal in size, evenly spaced and aligned; readouts and dates are centred under their faces; digit positions stay fixed as the readouts change (no sideways jitter between consecutive frames); nothing overlaps or is clipped.
A calm cinematic look a title designer would accept: deep blue-black background, consistent faces and typography, crisp anti-aliased hands and ticks, and no motion other than the clocks and playhead.

title: Parallax product film with named easings and freeze holds
prompt:
Animate a 12-second product film for the Alpenglow Flask 750, an insulated steel bottle for hikers. Everything is drawn in code; no photos.

Format: 1280x720, 30 fps, exactly 12 s (360 frames).

Scene: a dusk sky (vertical gradient from #1E3A8A at the top to #F9A8D4 at the horizon) and three parallax layers drawn wider than the frame: a pale far mountain range, darker mid hills, and dark pine silhouettes along the bottom. The sky never moves. When the camera pans, the layers move left by different amounts: far range 80 px, mid hills 240 px, pines 480 px (ratio 1 : 3 : 6).

The flask: a rounded vertical body in deep teal #0F766E, about 170 × 400 px, with a lighter vertical highlight, a dark cap and a small white mountain logo on the body.

Timeline (u runs from 0 to 1 over each move; the easing functions are the standard ones from easings.net):
1. 0.0 to 4.0 s: camera pan; each layer's offset is its total shift × easeInOutSine(u). The headline 'Made for the last light.' fades in (linear) from 0.5 to 1.5 s at the top left.
2. 4.0 to 5.0 s: hold. Nothing on screen moves.
3. 5.0 to 6.0 s: the flask drops in from above the frame to its resting place, centred at x = 640 with its base on the ground, using easeOutBack (c1 = 1.70158), so it overshoots below its rest position by about 10% of the drop and settles back. An elliptical ground shadow under it grows as it lands.
4. 6.0 to 7.0 s: three callouts pop in at 6.0, 6.25 and 6.5 s, each scaling from 0 to 100% over 0.4 s with easeOutBack from its anchor dot on the flask, with a thin leader line to a label chip: 'Cold 24 h' (upper body, label on the left), 'Hot 12 h' (middle, label on the right), '750 ml · 410 g' (base, label on the left).
5. 7.0 to 8.0 s: hold. Nothing moves.
6. 8.0 to 10.0 s: the headline and callouts fade out over 8.0 to 8.3 s; from 8.0 to 9.0 s the flask slides left to x = 420 with easeInOutCubic while the camera pans back halfway (every layer returns to half of its total shift, also easeInOutCubic); from 8.8 to 9.8 s the price '$39' counts up from $0 in whole dollars (rounded down) with easeOutExpo, large on the right, with 'Alpenglow Flask 750' above it.
7. 10.0 to 11.0 s: a pill button 'Shop at alpenglow.co' rises 20 px and fades in below the price, easeOutCubic.
8. 11.0 to 12.0 s: hold on the end card. Nothing moves.

Keep all text inside a 64 px margin. Use Inter and a palette of dusk sky, violet mountains, teal flask and white text.

rubric.criterion: Parallax pan: comparing frames at 0.0 and 4.5 s, the far range moved about 80 px left, the mid hills about 240 px and the pines about 480 px (ratio about 1:3:6, ±15%) while the sky is unchanged; at 2.0 s each layer is about halfway (easeInOutSine midpoint).
The three holds are true freezes: the frames at 4.1 and 4.9 s, at 7.1 and 7.9 s, and at 11.1 and 11.9 s are identical or nearly so (no drifting, twinkling or breathing elements).

The flask drop uses easeOutBack: no flask before 5.0 s; at about 5.58 s the flask sits clearly below its final resting position (an overshoot of roughly 10% of the drop distance); by 6.0 s it rests on the ground centred near x = 640.
The flask matches the brief: rounded teal body (about #0F766E) with a lighter vertical highlight, a dark cap and a small white mountain logo, standing on an elliptical ground shadow.

Callouts: at about 6.15 s only the first callout has started; at about 6.4 s the second is present and the third not yet; by 7.0 s all three read exactly 'Cold 24 h' (left, upper body), 'Hot 12 h' (right, middle) and '750 ml · 410 g' (left, base), each with a leader line to a dot on the flask.
The price count-up follows easeOutExpo with rounding down: it reads $0 or is just appearing at about 8.8 s, $29 (±1) at 9.0 s, $37 (±1) at 9.3 s, and $39 from about 9.8 s on.

Between 8.0 and 9.0 s the flask slides left to about x = 420 while the layers pan back to half their shift (at 10 s the pines are about 240 px left of their starting place); the headline and callouts are gone by 8.3 s.

Text: the headline 'Made for the last light.' appears at the top left during the pan; the end card shows 'Alpenglow Flask 750', a large '$39' on the right and the pill button 'Shop at alpenglow.co' below the price, which rose into place between 10.0 and 11.0 s.

All text stays at least about 64 px from the frame edges; callout chips and leader lines do not overlap each other or the logo; the end card is balanced with the flask on the left and the price block on the right.

A polished dusk look: smooth gradient sky, layered violet mountains with clear depth (lighter far, darker near), crisp anti-aliased shapes, and motion that visibly follows the named easings rather than linear moves.

title: Before/after color-grade wipe with exact divider timing
prompt:
Make a 12-second before/after comparison video for Lumen, a color-grading app, showing what its Dusk look does to a harbour scene. There are no photos: draw one procedural scene in code (a sky with a low sun, a skyline of at least 12 buildings with window grids, a pier with 4 lamp posts, and water in the lower third that reflects the skyline) and render it in two versions with identical geometry:
- BEFORE: flat and dull: desaturated (almost grey-blue), low contrast, windows and lamps unlit, no glow.
- AFTER: the graded look: teal shadows, warm orange highlights around the sun and the horizon, lit yellow windows and lamps with a soft glow, clearly higher contrast.
The versions must line up exactly: every building edge continues straight across the divider.

Format: 1280x720, 30 fps, exactly 12 s (360 frames).

Divider: a vertical 4 px white line across the full height at x = X(t). Left of it shows BEFORE and right of it shows AFTER. At its vertical centre sits a 48 px white circular handle with two small dark chevrons (◀ ▶). Just above the handle a small chip reads 'AFTER N%', where N = round(100 × (1280 − X) / 1280).
Badges: a pill 'BEFORE' at the top left and a pill 'AFTER' at the top right. Each belongs to its own version, so the wipe clips them: a badge is visible only where its side is showing.

Divider timeline (u runs 0 to 1 over each move):
- 0.0 to 1.0 s: full BEFORE (X = 1280, divider off-screen).
- 1.0 to 2.5 s: X from 1280 to 640, easeOutCubic.
- 2.5 to 4.0 s: hold at 640. During this hold three adjustment chips appear at the bottom right one after another at 2.7, 2.85 and 3.0 s: 'Contrast +38', 'Warmth +22', 'Shadows → Teal'; they fade out from 3.8 to 4.0 s.
- 4.0 to 5.5 s: 640 to 320, easeInOutCubic.
- 5.5 to 7.0 s: 320 to 960, easeInOutCubic.
- 7.0 to 8.0 s: 960 to 640, easeInOutCubic.
- 8.0 to 9.0 s: hold at 640.
- 9.0 to 10.5 s: 640 to 0, easeInCubic (the divider accelerates out to the left).
- 10.5 to 12.0 s: full AFTER with no divider; the caption 'Graded in one click with Lumen' fades in at the bottom centre from 10.5 to 11.0 s and stays.

Style: Inter; white UI elements with a subtle shadow so they read on both versions. The scene itself is still; only the divider and UI move.

rubric.criterion: Divider positions at the stops match (±10 px) with matching chips: x = 640 and 'AFTER 50%' at 3.0 s; 320 and 'AFTER 75%' at 5.5 s; 960 and 'AFTER 25%' at 7.0 s; 640 and 'AFTER 50%' at 8.5 s.

In-between positions follow the named easings (±15 px): about x = 830 with 'AFTER 35%' at 1.5 s (easeOutCubic, already most of the way), about x = 640 at 6.25 s (midpoint of the 320 to 960 move), and about x = 560 with 'AFTER 56%' at 9.75 s (easeInCubic, still slow).
Identical geometry: at 3.0 s building edges, the horizon, the pier and the reflections line up exactly across the divider; only the grading differs between the halves.

The two grades are distinct as briefed: the BEFORE side is desaturated, low-contrast and unlit; the AFTER side has teal shadows, warm orange highlights near the sun and horizon, and lit yellow windows and lamps with a soft glow.
The scene contains the requested elements: a low sun, at least 12 buildings with window grids, a pier with 4 lamp posts, and water in the lower third reflecting the skyline.

Start and end states: the frame at 0.5 s shows only BEFORE (no divider, no AFTER badge); the frame at 11.5 s shows only AFTER with the caption 'Graded in one click with Lumen' and no divider or BEFORE badge.

Badges belong to their sides: both badges are visible at 5.5 s; the AFTER badge is still visible at 7.0 s; at about 10.4 s (divider near x = 120) the BEFORE badge is cut by the divider rather than floating on top of the AFTER side.

Divider UI and chips: a 4 px white full-height line, a round white handle with two chevrons at the vertical centre and the 'AFTER N%' chip above it; the chips 'Contrast +38', 'Warmth +22', 'Shadows → Teal' appear in that order (only the first at about 2.75 s) and are gone by 4.0 s.
UI stays legible over both versions (shadow or contrast), the percentage chip moves with the handle without colliding with the badges, and nothing is clipped at the frame edges.
The AFTER version looks like a professional cinematic grade a colorist would show in a product demo, and the divider moves smoothly without jitter between consecutive frames.

title: Seamless 60 fps orbital rosette loop
prompt:
Create a seamlessly looping piece of generative motion art called Orbital Rosette for a gallery screen that plays it on repeat.

Format: 1080x1080, 60 fps, exactly 6 s (360 frames). Frame n shows the state at t = n / 60 s. The loop period is 6 s, so the frame that would follow the last one is identical to frame 0.

Composition, centred at (540, 540):
- Background: a static radial gradient from #111436 at the centre to #05060F at the corners.
- Eight concentric rings of dots at radii 70, 120, 170, 220, 270, 320, 370 and 420 px. Ring i (i = 1 innermost to 8 outermost) carries 6 × i evenly spaced dots. Faint thin circles show the ring paths.
- In each ring one dot is the marker: larger (about 11 px radius), with a white core and a coloured glow. At t = 0 every marker is at 12 o'clock, straight above the centre.
- Ring i rotates at constant angular speed through exactly 9 − i full turns per loop: ring 1 turns 8 times, ring 8 once. Odd rings turn clockwise, even rings counter-clockwise. No easing.
- A chain: a 2 px line from the centre to the ring 1 marker, then from marker to marker out to ring 8.
- Each marker leaves a fading trail along its ring covering its last 0.2 s of motion. The trails must be continuous across the loop point, so frame 0 already shows full trails.
- Core: a glowing filled circle at the centre with radius 36 + 8 × sin(2π t / 2) px, so it breathes three times per loop.
- Colour: the dots, marker glows and chain use hues that rotate through the full colour wheel exactly once per loop, with ring i offset by 45 × (i − 1) degrees from ring 1, so at any moment the rings form a rainbow.

All 360 frames must be distinct (true 60 fps, no duplicated frames), and nothing may pause, reset or jump at the loop point.

rubric.criterion: The loop is seamless: the last frame (about 5.983 s) differs from the first frame by one small motion step, like any pair of consecutive frames, with no jump, fade or reset; frame 0 already shows full marker trails.
At t = 0 all eight markers are at 12 o'clock, so the chain is a straight vertical line from the centre upward.
At 1.5 s (frame 90) the markers form the predicted pinwheel (±10°): rings 1 and 5 at 12 o'clock, rings 2 and 6 at 3 o'clock, rings 3 and 7 at 6 o'clock, rings 4 and 8 at 9 o'clock.
At 3.0 s (frame 180) the markers of rings 1, 3, 5 and 7 are at 12 o'clock and those of rings 2, 4, 6 and 8 at 6 o'clock (±10°), so the chain zigzags along the vertical axis.

Directions and speeds: between two consecutive frames (e.g. frames 60 and 61) odd rings move clockwise and even rings counter-clockwise, and inner rings turn through larger angles than outer ones (ring 1 about 8° per frame, ring 8 about 1°).
True 60 fps: consecutive frames always differ (decode with ffmpeg and check several pairs, such as frames 0/1, 101/102 and 358/359); there are no duplicated frames.
Structure: eight rings with 6, 12, 18, … dots (count at least the inner three rings), faint ring paths, one larger marker per ring, and a chain from the centre through the markers in ring order.
The core breathes on schedule: largest (about 44 px radius) at 0.5, 2.5 and 4.5 s and smallest (about 28 px) at 1.5, 3.5 and 5.5 s.
Colours rotate once per loop: each ring's hue at 3.0 s is roughly complementary to its hue at 0.0 s, the rings form a rainbow at every moment, and the hues at the end match the start.
Gallery-quality motion art: glowing anti-aliased dots and trails, a balanced composition fully inside the frame, and smooth motion without strobing.

title: Insertion sort explainer with an algorithm-driven timeline
prompt:
Make an explainer video for a computer-science course that visualizes insertion sort on the array [6, 3, 8, 1, 7, 2, 9, 4]. The timeline is fully determined by the algorithm, so follow these rules exactly.

Format: 1280x720, 30 fps. The duration follows from the rules below: compute it, it is not given.

Visuals: eight vertical bars in eight evenly spaced slots along a baseline, each bar's height proportional to its value, the value printed in or on each bar, and the slot index 0 to 7 under each slot. A HUD at the top shows 'Pass i of 7', 'Comparisons: C' and 'Shifts: S', plus 'key = k' during a pass.

Algorithm (standard insertion sort): for i = 1 to 7: key = a[i], j = i − 1; while j ≥ 0 and a[j] > key: a[j + 1] = a[j] (a shift) and j = j − 1; finally a[j + 1] = key. A comparison is one evaluation of a[j] > key with j ≥ 0; nothing is counted when j reaches −1.

Timeline:
- 0.0 to 1.0 s: intro: the title 'Insertion sort, step by step' and the bars rise into place.
- Then each pass i runs back to back:
  - Lift, 0.4 s: 'Pass i of 7' updates as it starts; the key bar turns orange and rises 120 px above its slot (ease-out).
  - Each comparison, 0.5 s: C increments as it starts and the compared bar a[j] gets a yellow outline for the whole 0.5 s. If a[j] > key, during the second half (0.25 s) that bar slides one slot right, S increments as the slide starts, and the lifted key moves one slot left above it. Otherwise nothing moves and the comparisons for this pass end.
  - Drop, 0.4 s: the key drops into its slot and returns to the normal colour; the bars in slots 0 to i are now tinted green as the sorted prefix.
- After pass 7: a 0.2 s pause, then a victory sweep in which the bars flash bright green one at a time from left to right, 0.1 s apart (8 flashes). 0.1 s after the last flash starts, the caption 'Sorted in C comparisons and S shifts' appears with the real totals; hold for exactly 2.0 s more, then the video ends.

Style: a clean dark-slate look, Inter or Roboto, blue-grey unsorted bars, orange key, yellow comparison outline and green sorted bars; eased motion that never teleports.

rubric.criterion: Final state: the last frames show the bars in the order 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, all green, the caption reads exactly 'Sorted in 18 comparisons and 13 shifts', and the HUD shows Comparisons: 18 and Shifts: 13.
Intro and ending timing: the title 'Insertion sort, step by step' is visible at about 0.5 s; the caption is absent at 16.4 s and present from about 16.7 s; the video is 18.6 s long (±0.1 s).

Pass 3 at about 5.1 s: 'Pass 3 of 7', key = 1 lifted above slot 1, bar 3 in slot 0 outlined as the compared bar, bars 6 and 8 already moved to slots 2 and 3, and the HUD reads Comparisons: 5 and Shifts: 3.
Pass 5 lift at about 7.9 s: 'Pass 5 of 7', key = 2 lifted above slot 5, Comparisons: 7, Shifts: 5, and the other bars read 1, 3, 6, 7, 8 in slots 0 to 4 (green) and 9, 4 in slots 6 and 7.
A pass without a shift: at about 11.6 s (pass 6, key = 9) bar 8 is outlined as it is compared, nothing slides, and the HUD reads Comparisons: 13 and Shifts: 9.
Pass 7 at about 14.3 s: key = 4 lifted, bar 6 outlined as the compared bar, bars 9, 8 and 7 already shifted right, and the HUD reads Comparisons: 17 and Shifts: 12.
Shifts are animated slides: a frame at about 4.35 s (second half of pass 3's first comparison) shows bar 8 between slots 2 and 3 and the lifted key between slots rather than a jump cut.

Colour states follow the brief: the key is orange while lifted, the compared bar has a yellow outline, the sorted prefix is green after each drop, and the final sweep lights the bars one by one from left to right between about 15.8 and 16.6 s.
Bars sit in eight evenly spaced slots with index labels 0 to 7; values are legible on every bar, including the shortest (1); the lifted key never collides with the HUD; nothing is clipped.
Teaching-quality design: a consistent palette (blue-grey, orange, yellow, green), a readable HUD with clear hierarchy, and smooth eased motion throughout.

title: Bouncing-ball physics explainer with live graph and HUD
prompt:
Create a physics explainer video of a ball dropped onto a floor, with a live height graph and exact numbers, for a high-school physics channel.

Format: 1280x720, 30 fps, exactly 11 s (330 frames).

Physics (no air drag, g = 9.81 m/s², mass 0.5 kg): the ball is held with its bottom at height h = 8.00 m above the floor until t = 0.50 s, then released from rest. At each impact it rebounds with 0.75 times its impact speed (coefficient of restitution 0.75). When a rebound speed would be below 0.5 m/s, the ball stops on the floor and stays at rest. Every impact counts as a bounce, including the last one. Compute the motion analytically from the impact times (not with a coarse numerical integrator), so values are right to two decimals.

Left half: a tower view with the floor line, a vertical ruler from 0 to 8 m with a tick and label every metre, and the ball (radius 18 px) drawn to scale at 60 px per metre, its bottom touching the floor when h = 0. No squash or stretch.

Right half: a live graph of h (m, 0 to 8) against t (s, 0 to 11) with labelled axes and gridlines; the curve is drawn only up to the current time, with a dot at the current point.

HUD above the graph, updated every frame, all values with two decimals: 't = 2.50 s', 'h = … m', 'v = … m/s' (signed, positive upward), 'Bounces: N' and 'Energy: … J' (total mechanical energy m·g·h + ½·m·v²). Once the ball has stopped, show an 'At rest' badge. Use fixed-width digit cells so the numbers never jitter sideways.

Also draw a vertical energy bar split into potential energy (blue, bottom) and kinetic energy (orange, top), whose total height is proportional to the total energy (full height = 39.24 J).

Style: clean textbook graphics on a light background, Inter, and one accent colour for the ball.

rubric.criterion: HUD at 1.40 s: h = 4.03 m, v = −8.83 m/s, Bounces: 0, Energy: 39.24 J, and the ball's bottom is at about the 4 m mark on the ruler.
HUD at 2.50 s: h = 4.23 m, v = 2.30 m/s (positive), Bounces: 1, Energy: 22.07 J; and at 4.00 s: h = 1.70 m, v = 4.03 m/s, Bounces: 2, Energy: 12.42 J (±0.01 on each value).
HUD at 6.00 s: h = 0.88 m, v = −3.25 m/s, Bounces: 3, Energy: 6.98 J (±0.01).

The ball stops after exactly 12 bounces at about 9.12 s: from about 9.2 s to the end the HUD reads Bounces: 12, h = 0.00 m, v = 0.00 m/s, Energy: 0.00 J with the 'At rest' badge; at 8.9 s it is still bouncing (no badge, Bounces: 10).
The ball is held still at 8 m until 0.5 s (the tower looks the same at 0.1 and 0.45 s), and the first impact is at about 1.78 s (Bounces changes from 0 to 1 between 1.75 and 1.80 s).
Rebound peaks are right: the first rebound peaks at 4.50 m at about 2.73 s and the second at about 2.53 m at about 4.41 s; the ball on the ruler and the graph curve agree with these heights.

The graph draws live: a frame at about 3.0 s shows the curve only from 0 to 3 s (the hold, the falling parabola and part of the first bounce arc) with the dot at the current height; the final graph shows a decaying series of parabolic arcs ending flat at 0.
The energy bar has a blue potential part and an orange kinetic part; its total height is full at the start, constant during each flight and drops at each bounce to about 56% of its previous height.

The tower (ruler 0 to 8 m with metre labels, floor, ball) and the graph (axes 0 to 11 s and 0 to 8 m, gridlines) are legible and aligned, the HUD digits do not shift sideways between frames, and nothing overlaps or is clipped.
Clean textbook-quality graphics: light background, consistent Inter typography, one accent colour for the ball, crisp anti-aliased curves.

title: Recreate an animated revenue dashboard
prompt:
Recreate this animated dashboard as an MP4: 1280x720, 30 fps, exactly 10 s (300 frames). The attached frames frame_1.png to frame_6.png were taken at 1.8, 3.1, 4.2, 5.2, 6.7 and 9.0 s. Measure positions, sizes and colours from them; the motion between them is not visible in stills, so follow the timeline below exactly.

Content: the header 'Q3 Revenue Review' with the subtitle 'Northwind Outfitters · weekly revenue, July to September' and a 'FY2026 Q3' pill; three cards: a line chart 'Weekly revenue ($k)' with gridlines at 0, 100, 200, 300 and 400 and weeks W1 to W13 with the values 212, 228, 219, 246, 262, 251, 280, 297, 289, 318, 336, 352 and 371; a 'Total revenue' KPI card; and a 'Quarterly target' donut card. Font: Inter (Bold, SemiBold, Medium, Regular). Main colours: background #0B1220, cards #111A2E with a 1 px #1E2A44 border, line #38BDF8, donut #A78BFA over a #1E2A44 track, delta chip text #22C55E, annotation #F59E0B.

Timeline (u runs 0 to 1 over each interval):
- 0.0 to 0.8 s: the three cards rise 24 px and fade in, 0.6 s each with easeOutCubic, starting at 0.0, 0.1 and 0.2 s (chart card, KPI card, donut card). The header is static from the first frame.
- 0.8 to 2.8 s: the KPI counts from $0.00M to $3.66M (two decimals) with easeOutCubic; from 2.8 to 3.2 s the '+18.4% vs Q2' chip fades in.
- 1.0 to 4.0 s: the line and the gradient area under it are revealed from left to right by a vertical edge moving at constant speed from W1 to W13; each week's dot appears when the edge reaches it.
- 4.0 to 4.4 s: the '$371k' chip above the last point fades in while scaling from 60% to 100% with easeOutBack.
- 4.4 to 6.0 s: the donut arc grows clockwise from 12 o'clock to 86.1% of the circle (3.661 / 4.25) with easeInOutCubic, its centre label counting in whole percent; from 6.0 to 6.3 s '$3.66M of $4.25M' fades in below it.
- 6.4 to 7.0 s: the callout 'Summer sale +12%' drops 24 px into place above W8 while fading in (easeOutCubic); 6.6 to 7.2 s: a dashed amber guide draws downward from the callout to the axis; 7.0 to 7.2 s: an amber ring fades in around the W8 point.
- 7.2 to 10.0 s: hold.

rubric.criterion: The static layout matches the reference frames: header with title, subtitle and FY2026 Q3 pill; the chart card on the left and the two stacked cards on the right at the same positions and sizes, with rounded corners, thin borders and the dark palette.
The chart matches: gridlines and labels 0 to 400, W1 to W13 labels, the sky-blue line through the given values with ring-style dots, and the gradient area fading toward the axis.

The KPI card (large '$3.66M', green '+18.4% vs Q2' chip) and the donut card (violet round-capped arc from 12 o'clock over a dark track, '86%' in the centre, '$3.66M of $4.25M' below) match in position, size, colour and typography.
The line reveal and KPI follow the timeline: at 1.8 s only W1 to W4 are drawn (the edge just past W4) and the KPI reads about $3.20M; at 3.1 s W1 to W9 are drawn and the KPI reads $3.66M.
The donut follows easeInOutCubic: empty before 4.4 s, about 43% at 5.2 s (label and arc agree), 86% from 6.0 s on.
The intro exists: frames between about 0.1 and 0.5 s show the cards rising and fading in, staggered with the chart card first, and the KPI number and the line are absent at 0.5 s.
Chips pop on time: the '+18.4% vs Q2' chip fades in around 2.8 to 3.2 s, and the '$371k' chip is part-transparent and near full size at 4.2 s, fully shown from 4.4 s.

The annotation sequence matches: at 6.7 s the 'Summer sale +12%' callout is still dropping in and the dashed guide has only just started; by 7.2 s the guide reaches the axis and the amber ring surrounds the W8 point; everything then holds to 10 s.

title: Recreate an onboarding carousel with parallax
prompt:
Recreate this onboarding carousel animation for the habit app Tempo as an MP4: 1080x1080, 30 fps, exactly 12 s (360 frames). The attached frames frame_1.png to frame_6.png were taken at 1.5, 3.4, 3.7, 7.5, 9.0 and 10.2 s. Measure the layout, sizes and shapes from them, and follow the motion rules below exactly.

Slides (title / two body lines / background / accent):
1. 'Plan your week' / 'Drag tasks onto the days that suit you' + 'and Tempo fills in the rest.' / #EEF2FF / #6366F1
2. 'Track every habit' / 'Tick off habits in one tap and watch' + 'your weekly progress grow.' / #ECFDF5 / #10B981
3. 'Celebrate streaks' / 'Hit a seven-day streak and unlock' + 'new themes for your planner.' / #FFF7ED / #F97316
Each slide has an illustration built from simple shapes in its accent colour on a pale accent circle (a calendar card, a habit checklist card, a star with the number 7 and sparkles). Titles are Inter Bold 60 px in #0F172A and body lines Inter Regular 30 px in #475569. Fixed chrome: a logo dot and 'Tempo' (Inter Bold) at the top left, 'Skip' (Inter Medium, #64748B) at the top right, page indicator dots and a pill button at the bottom.

Motion:
- Slide changes run from 3.0 to 4.0 s and from 7.0 to 8.0 s with p = easeInOutCubic(u). Let s be the slide position: 0 on slide 1, 1 on slide 2, 2 on slide 3, and k + p during a change away from slide index k.
- Parallax: slide k (k = 0, 1, 2) is offset horizontally from its resting place by (k − s) × 1080 px × factor, with factor 1.25 for the illustration, 1.0 for the title and 0.85 for the body text, so the illustration leads and the body lags.
- The background and the accent-coloured elements (logo dot, button, active dot) blend linearly in RGB between the two slides' colours by the fractional part of s.
- Page indicator: #CBD5E1 dots 14 px tall with 12 px gaps; dot k is 14 + 30 × max(0, 1 − |s − k|) px wide and its colour is blended toward accent k by the same amount; the row stays centred.
- 'Skip' fades out as s goes from 1 to 2.
- Button label (white Inter SemiBold 30): 'Next' fades out as s goes from 1.0 to 1.5 and 'Get started' fades in from 1.5 to 2.0.
- Press at 10.0 s: the button scales to 94% around its centre over 0.12 s (easeOutQuad) and back to 100% by 10.4 s (easeOutQuad), while a white ripple clipped to the button grows from its centre (radius 20 + 300 × easeOutCubic(u) px over 0.6 s) with opacity 0.35 × (1 − u).
- Everything else holds still.

rubric.criterion: The rest states match frames 1 and 5 (1.5 and 9.0 s): background colours, illustration size and position, title and body positions and sizes, top bar, page indicator and button.

The illustrations match: a calendar card with an accent header, two binder tabs and a 3x4 grid with one accent cell; a checklist card with two filled check circles, one empty circle and three progress bars of decreasing fill; an accent star with a white 7 and three sparkles; each on a pale accent circle.
The chrome matches: logo dot and 'Tempo' at the top left, 'Skip' at the top right, a page indicator whose active dot is stretched into a pill, and a wide pill button with a white label.

Parallax during the first change: at 3.4 s slide 1's illustration has moved further left than its title, which has moved further than its body (about 346, 276 and 235 px), with slide 2's body text entering at the right edge; at 3.7 s slide 2 is nearly in place with its illustration still further right than its text.

Blending mid-change: at 7.5 s the background, button and logo dot are halfway blends of the slide 2 and slide 3 colours, the indicator shows two half-stretched dots, 'Skip' is half transparent, and the button shows no label (between 'Next' and 'Get started').
Slide timing: slide 1 rests until 3.0 s, slide 2 from 4.0 to 7.0 s and slide 3 from 8.0 s on; the button reads 'Next' on slides 1 and 2 and 'Get started' on slide 3; 'Skip' is gone on slide 3.
The press is visible: at 10.2 s the button is slightly smaller than at rest with a lighter ripple spread across it, and it is back to normal by about 10.6 s.
